Galvanostatic discharge and charge of the Li and Na half cells while the beam is on
The product is a two-phase mixture of cubic Co3O4 (Fd-3m) and cubic CoO (Fm-3m), about 79:21 by weight
The oxide is mesoporous: type IV isotherm, BET area 45 m2/g, pore volume 0.172 cm3/g
Against lithium: 1330 mA h/g first discharge, 871 reversible, still ~850 after 40 cycles
Against sodium: 866 mA h/g first discharge but only 472 reversible, decaying to ~65 by cycle 40
Lithiation drives the crystalline oxide fully amorphous and charging does not bring the crystallinity back
Sodiation only dims the same reflections slightly and shifts none of them, so little of the oxide reacts
Lithiation reduces Co towards the metal; recharging returns it only to a CoO-like state, not to pristine PCO
Sodiation leaves the Co valence and the Co coordination shells essentially as in the pristine oxide
Lithiation fills the large pores and creates new fine scatterers, and neither recovers on charge

nodes.label: The difference is the extent of the conversion reaction: lithium drives it to completion, sodium barely starts it
Sodium cannot strip oxygen from Co3O4 and stays largely un-oxidised, whereas it does attack the softer sulfide sublattice
The porous oxide serves as a good lithium-ion anode and a poor sodium-ion anode

notes: Two parallel spine branches, Li and Na, meeting at the mechanism identification. Lost: the EXAFS fitting table and the Co3S4 electrochemistry, which the packet does not carry. Audits: the SEM (o4) does not resolve the 10-20 nm particles the text claims, and TGA (o2) shows ~4 wt% undecomposed MOF still in the powder. The in operando SXRD (o9) shows the Li-cell reflections gone around 1 V, earlier than the 0.01 V endpoint the text names. Packet defect: the OCR reads the panel letter 'd' as 'p' in four figures (F2d, F3d, F5d, F6d), each flagged as an OCR/detector disagreement; the detector letter is the right one in all four.

changes: o12 image_note replaced with the numbers actually on F5d: OCV white line ~1.49 against ~1.30 for every cycled state, with the cycled curves lying on the Co3O4 reference. The old note called the OCV difference 'a little sharper', which understated it; the claim that nothing approaches Co foil is unchanged and still correct.
notes corrected: it claimed the SAXS line-profile panels F3b/F3d were not carried, but they are in the packet and o8 cites and reads both.

panel_checks.note: F1d is the SEM, data bar 'ANL-EMC 15.0kV 8.3mm x70.0k SE(M)' with a 500 nm scale. It shows interconnected rough blocks of roughly 100-200 nm; surface texture is visible but no 10-20 nm nanograins are resolved. The audit is fair and image_support=partial is right.

F4a is the Li/PCO in operando SXRD waterfall over 16-21 deg with the 0.1 C voltage profile co-plotted against time (0-25 h). The 16.4 and 19.2 deg peaks are strong at t = 0 and flat from about 5-6 h, i.e. near 1 V on the co-plotted curve, well before the 0.01 V endpoint, and they never return through the charge to 3 V at 24 h. Both the claim and its audit note are what the panel shows.

F5d is the Na/PCO XANES (caption: 'typical XANES spectrum at different charge/discharge states of Na/PCO cell'), with Co foil, CoO and Co3O4 references drawn in. The four cycled traces are bunched and lie on the Co3O4 reference, far from Co foil, as the node claims. The one correction is that the OCV trace stands further off than the note allowed; the note has been tightened.

review.audit_summary: Three audits (o4, o2/n27, and the early-peak-loss note inside o9), comfortably under budget and each one changing support. All three are of the 'figure does not resolve what the text claims' or 'figure shows more than the text says' kind, not contradictions, and the graph states them that way: o4 carries image_support=partial and a qualifies edge rather than contradicts; n27 is a DSC/limitation bounding the phase claim n10; the o9 note records that the reflections vanish near 1 V rather than at the 0.01 V endpoint the text names, which sharpens n14 without overturning it.
